name: arp-2600
description:
arp-2600.tap: a four-voice synth after the ARP 2600.

The 2600 is semi-modular: with no patch cords in, its modules are joined by
internal ("normalled") connections, each with a slider.  This file is that
normalled patch, slider for slider:

  VCO-1 (saw, square)            FM from sample & hold, ADSR, VCO-2 sine
  VCO-2 (sine, tri, saw, pulse)  FM from sample & hold, ADSR, VCO-1 square;
                                 pulse width modulated by noise
  VCO-3 (saw, pulse)             FM from noise, ADSR, VCO-2 sine
  ring modulator                 VCO-1 saw x VCO-2 sine
  noise generator                white to pink to low-frequency
  VCF mixer                      ring mod, VCO-1 square, VCO-2 pulse,
                                 VCO-3 saw, noise
  VCF                            cutoff from keyboard, ADSR, VCO-2 sine
  VCA                            audio from VCF and ring mod; gain from the
                                 AR and ADSR envelopes
  spring reverb                  on the output mix

The VCF is the ARP 4012, a copy of Moog's transistor ladder, modelled by
`ladder_lowpass` in kit.tap.  It self-oscillates at full resonance.

A real 2600 plays one note (two with the 3620 keyboard).  Here four of them
share one front panel.  Play it with `note_on` and `note_off` (a
music_note; pitch is a MIDI note number, velocity 0..1).  One note-on and
one note-off per block.

Not modelled: the patch points themselves, the preamp and envelope
follower, the lag processor, voltage processors and electronic switch.
